summary: SSE connection closes silently after gradual per-token latency escalation on long-context requests
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports SSE chat sessions disconnecting without a final token or error after ~20-40s of generation. This is distinct from abrupt 502/503 bursts; it follows a gradual increase in per-token latency during long-context conversations (context ~30k-60k tokens).

Impact: Several WaveForms AI production chat endpoints experienced silent stream closures across multiple hosts in us-west; client observed no final [DONE] and socket closed by remote side. Multiple conversations impacted, intermittent but reproducible with long histories. Customer's user-facing sessions dropped ~0.5% of requests in the last 24h with elevated latency tail.

Environment: Dedicated pool (dfw-dedicated-1) serving redwood-1-7b-v2, autoscaler enabled, prefix/KV caching turned on. Traffic originates from WaveForms AI via our private VPC peering.

Observed behavior: Token emission rate slows gradually (per-token latency climbs from ~30ms to ~400ms over ~30s) and then connection terminates silently. No consistent 5xx in front-end logs; gateway logs show a TCP FIN from client or proxy soon after latency exceeds ~350ms per token.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use WaveForms AI request shape: long conversation ~35k tokens, prompt + user history + system messages.
2) POST to /v1/chat/stream with SSE header and prefer chunked streaming.
3) Observe tokens streaming at first normal rate; after ~10-40s tokens slow progressively.
4) Eventually SSE connection closes without final data/event and client sees remote close or socket reset.
logs: gateway/us-west-2 - 2026-03-09T18:12:41Z - upstream write error: write tcp 10.0.12.45:443->10.8.7.3:53212: write: broken pipe

serving-runtime/worker-az3 - 2026-03-09T18:12:39Z - kv_cache: eviction triggered for prefix_id=0x7f2b after memory pressure

investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Tier 1 support: reproduced with customer request shape. No immediate 5xx from gateway; frontdoor reported client-side FIN. Correlated timing: a background autoscale activity and a prefix KV eviction happened within the same second token latency crossed 350ms. Hypothesis A: progressive KV cache misses cause increasing generation latency (long context causes larger KV working set). Hypothesis B: autoscaler/eviction or worker swap causes in-flight token emission pauses that look like progressive slowdown to clients and trigger proxy timeouts.

Action taken so far: - Captured p99 token latency across workers and request IDs. - Increased streaming keepalive to 60s on the customer's ingress path as a mitigation. - Routed a small percentage of customer traffic to a warm pool (no autoscale) which reduced occurrences. - Reproduced locally with match of context and observed KV eviction when simulated memory cap.

Next steps: SRE to instrument per-request kv_cache hit/miss metrics and per-token CPU stalls. Runtime team to add guardrails to prevent evictions during active streams (prefer background eviction windows) and to avoid draining warm workers while requests are in-flight. Engineering to review autoscaler thresholds for dedicated pools.

resolution:
Workaround: routed WaveForms AI traffic to warm pool and increased proxy keepalive to 60s; reduced customer-facing failures immediately. Permanent fix: merged change to serving-runtime to avoid prefix/KV eviction when active_streams > 0 (PR #842). Canaried to two hosts in dfw-dedicated-1; metrics in first 12h show p99 token latency reduced and no silent closes in test samples.

Follow-ups: 1) Add kv_cache hit/miss tracing per-request and expose streaming token latency percentiles in Console. 2) Autoscaler: add a protective 'do not scale down if active_streams > 0' flag for dedicated pools. 3) Postmortem owners: Diego Alvarez (runtime) and Priya Shah (SRE).
